$schema_notes: SHARED ACCEPT/REJECT CORPUS FOR THE AGENT LAUNCH POLICY VALIDATOR.
Two independent implementations validate ~/scripts/agent-launch.yml:
- task_dispatcher.cli.validate_launch_policy()          (Python, this repo)
- cloudcli-plugin-task-queue src/launch-policy.ts       (TypeScript)
The TS file carries a comment saying the Python side 'must keep computing this the
same way'. That is a comment where a test should be, and the two have already
disagreed once: Python called .resolve() on the project root while TypeScript did a
plain join, so with a symlink anywhere on the path Python rejected entries the
plugin accepted. On forge that did not merely reject an entry — LAUNCH_POLICY is
built at import, so it made the dispatcher module fail to import on every tick.
THIS FILE IS THE CONTRACT. Both suites load it and must agree, case for case, on
both the verdict AND the resolved values. Verdict alone is not enough: the .resolve()
divergence above changed what a spawn's cwd would be long before it changed any
accept/reject answer.
OWNED BY task-dispatcher, CONSUMED BY THE PLUGIN over raw.githubusercontent.com at
`main` — the same direction and mechanism as the task-queue vocabulary gate, so
there is one pattern in this fleet rather than two. A change here turns the plugin's
CI red on its next push; that is the alarm, not a malfunction.
{HOME} is substituted by each side with ITS OWN test home before validating, and in
the expected values too. It is a token rather than a literal path because Python
expands `~` against the ambient $HOME while the TypeScript side expands it against a
`home` argument — so a hardcoded path would make the two incomparable for exactly
the `~` cases that most need covering.
Adding a case here is how you pin a behaviour in both languages at once. Do not
delete a case to make a side pass; make the sides agree.

cases.name: minimal-valid-agent
cases.why: The ordinary entry. If this fails, nothing else here means anything.

cases.name: run-as-agent-with-launcher
cases.why: The steward shape. run_as_user and launcher travel together into a sudo argv.

cases.name: tilde-expands-to-an-absolute-path
cases.why: The live roster is written with `~`. Both sides must expand it, not reject it.

cases.name: dotdot-inside-the-root-is-normalised-not-rejected
cases.why: `..` that stays under the root is legal; the containment check must run AFTER normalisation on both sides, or one of them compares an unnormalised path.

cases.name: trailing-slash-normalises-away
cases.why: The resolved value becomes a spawn's cwd. Python's os.path.normpath strips a trailing separator and Node's path.normalize does NOT, so without this case the two sides silently produce different strings for the same input — the .resolve() divergence in a second costume.

cases.name: project-dir-equal-to-the-root-is-accepted
cases.why: The boundary of the containment check. A strict `is a descendant of` test rejects it; both sides intend to allow it.

cases.name: sibling-directory-sharing-a-name-prefix-is-rejected
cases.why: The containment check must be segment-wise, not a string prefix. `projects-evil` starts with `projects` and is not under it.

cases.name: dotdot-escaping-the-root-is-rejected
cases.why: The traversal this validator exists for: the value reaches a subprocess cwd.

cases.name: relative-project-dir-is-rejected
cases.why: A relative cwd would resolve against whatever the launching process happened to be in.

cases.name: unknown-key-rejects-the-whole-document
cases.why: An unrecognised key is a typo'd one. Ignoring it means honouring a roster whose author believes it says something it does not.

cases.name: run-as-user-without-a-launcher-is-rejected
cases.why: Half a run-as entry is how an agent gets launched as the caller while every log says otherwise (vikunja#404).

cases.name: launcher-dir-prefix-trap-is-rejected
cases.why: `/usr/local/sbin/forgery/` shares a prefix with `/usr/local/sbin/forge/` and is a different directory. The trailing separator in the constant is what closes this.

cases.name: launcher-with-dotdot-is-rejected
cases.why: sudoers pins the path, so this cannot widen what sudo runs — but a roster that reads as one thing and resolves to another must not validate.

cases.name: agent-name-with-a-dot-is-rejected
cases.why: The name is used to build paths on both sides.

cases.name: prototype-pollution-name-is-rejected
cases.why: JS-specific and free to close on both sides: `__proto__` as a key in an object literal is not an ordinary property, and a lookup by an agent name taken from task content must not reach an inherited member. The shared name regex rejects it because it does not start with a lowercase letter.

cases.name: empty-document-is-rejected
cases.why: An empty roster leaves run_as_user absent for EVERY agent, which is how steward gets launched as ted. Degrading to `{}` is the failure both loaders are built to refuse.

cases.name: one-bad-entry-rejects-the-whole-document
cases.why: A partially-honoured roster silently launches SOME agent the wrong way. Both sides must refuse the document, not skip the entry.

cases.name: multiple-valid-agents-all-resolve
cases.why: Guards against a loop that returns after its first entry.
